relevance_note: The paper describes identifiable individuals with SSADHD and ALDH5A1 variants, e.g. 'We identified 16 individuals in the BG-BCM cohort (Cases 1–16, Table 1) with possible or known SSADHD' plus 'eight unrelated individuals from the Boston Children’s Hospital SSADHD Biobank (Cases 17–24, Table 1)'.
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema and the rules; the Markdown full text was read by hand and Table 1 transcribed manually (no script was used). The file ends with the Publisher's note and contains no 'Supplementary material' section, so Supplementary Tables S1–S5 could not be read. Labels use the paper's own form 'Case N' (Table 1 column 'Case #'; text 'Case 2', 'Cases 1–16', 'Cases 17–24'). Table 1 has patients as rows, so spans run from the patient label through the relevant cell; the column header is quoted in the gene/transcript fields. The 'Age (y)' column is the age at genetic testing or Biobank sample collection (Methods 3.1: 'At the time of genetic testing or Biobank sample collection and analysis, participant ages ranged from 6 months to 44 years'); it is recorded in age_at_last_evaluation and converted (0.5 y -> P6M). is_proband is false for all 24 (nobody is called a proband; this is a cohort, not the single-patient case report of rule 5) and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is false because no earlier report of these patients is cited. Zygosity comes from Table 1's two allele columns (identical cells -> homozygous; two different variants -> compound heterozygous); only Case 2 is called 'compound heterozygous' in the text. variant_type, ACMG criteria and functional evidence are 'not reported' because variant classes are given only in general criteria ('resulted in a premature termination codon', 'occurred at a splice site'), never per variant. Pathogenicity is recorded only where the exact variant (the three novel variants) or the person's own variants (Cases 2 and 13) are called pathogenic. Case 11's two variants are only described as 'the same two variants' as his sister's, so his rows are left 'not reported' for pathogenicity; likewise Case 5's c.379_380del (p.Trp127ValfsTer8) is not the novel c.380G>A (p.Trp127Ter) carried by Case 12, so that classification was not transferred to him. The Table 1 symptom 'unsteady gait' was mapped to the checklist item ataxia. Normal findings (D-27) are recorded as excluded features naming the abnormality ruled out: 'no structural anomalies' and 'A dedicated renal ultrasound was normal' (Case 2), 'with normal MR spectroscopy' (Case 11), and 'normal female karyotype', 'creatine kinase (CK) level, and transferrin isoelectric focusing' (Case 13). Urine GHB values for Cases 17–24 are recorded as an observed feature 'urine GHB'; they exceed the paper's stated normal range (Table 1 note: 'GHB, normal value: 0–7 mmol/mol creatinine'). Not recorded: untargeted metabolomic z-score results (2-pyrrolidinone, 4-guanidinobutanoate, argininate, succinimide) as research biomarkers rather than clinical features; Case 13's 'paternally inherited deletion at 12q22.2' (authors: 'felt not to be clinically significant'); the study's search/inclusion criteria; Case 13's IVF and twin-pregnancy details. Table 1's 'Developmental delays' was not mapped to the checklist item 'gross or fine motor deficits' except for Case 13, whose motor delay is explicit ('delayed in the attainment of gross motor, fine motor, and speech milestones'); Case 11's 'non-verbal' (Table 1) was mapped to 'speech or language impairment'. Case 13's 'two electroencephalograms' with no abnormal EEG result is not evidence of 'EEG abnormality'. Relatives named only as obstetric background (Case 2's mother, Case 13's twin who died in utero) get no rows: the paper gives no individual-level fact about them. Contradictions in the paper: (1) 'four individuals harbored homozygous pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants' while Table 1 shows eight homozygous cases (1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 20, 22, 23); (2) 'This comprehensive review of sequencing data identified 14 individuals with biallelic variants in ALDH5A1' although 16 BG-BCM cases are listed (Cases 11 and 13 were tested elsewhere); (3) Case 13's first brain MRI was read as 'normal' but later reinterpretation noted subtle bilateral increased signal in the globus pallidus (recorded as observed); (4) the abstract says '16 patients with likely SSADHD' while 24 individuals are reported; (5) the same c.1323dup variant is printed with two different protein consequences (Case 6: 'p.Pro442AlafsTer19'; Case 21: 'p.Pro442AlafsTer18'). reports_individuals_with_tnfaip3_variant is true because every one of the 24 cases has individual-level detail.
